question.text: A stock exchange member fails to furnish required information to SEBI for 25 days under Section 23A of SCRA. Which statement best describes the penalty exposure for this single failure?

answer.text: Not less than Rs. 1 lakh, extendable up to Rs. 1 lakh per day during the continuing failure — i.e. up to Rs. 25 lakh for 25 days — subject to a maximum of Rs. 1 crore for the failure
Flat penalty of Rs. 1 lakh regardless of duration
Rs. 25,000 per day, up to Rs. 50 lakh
No penalty unless the failure exceeds 30 days

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 23A prescribes a penalty of not less than Rs. 1 lakh, which may extend to Rs. 1 lakh for each day during which the failure continues, subject to a maximum of Rs. 1 crore for each failure. For a 25-day failure, the per-day extension can reach 25 × Rs. 1 lakh = Rs. 25 lakh, within the Rs. 1 crore per-failure cap. The Trap: Rs. 25 lakh is the per-day extension amount for 25 days, not the statutory minimum. The minimum is Rs. 1 lakh; the per-day amount and the Rs. 1 crore cap define the upper end of the range. Note: The Rs. 1 crore ceiling is per failure, so distinct failures can produce separate penalty exposures within their own caps.
